did_you_know.text: Did you know? David describes Solomon as “young and inexperienced,” emphasizing that the task is great because the temple is not intended for a human being but for the Lord.
Did you know? David dedicated 3,000 talents of gold from Ophir and 7,000 talents of refined silver for overlaying the walls of the buildings.
Did you know? After detailing his own contributions, David asked the people who was willing to volunteer for the Lord and dedicate their gifts to the work of the temple.

Did you know? The leaders of Israel contributed to the work of the house of God 5,000 talents of gold and tens of thousands of darics, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.
Did you know? The people rejoiced not only because of the size of the contributions, but because they were given wholeheartedly; King David also rejoiced greatly.

Did you know? In his blessing, David presents a central principle: no one can give the Lord anything that did not come from Him in the first place—“Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from your hand.”

Did you know? David describes human life in this world as a time of pilgrimage and temporary residence, comparing its length to a passing shadow—a picture emphasizing the fleeting nature of human life.
Did you know? David asks the Lord to preserve the people’s willingness to give and the integrity of their thoughts, so that their enthusiasm will not be merely momentary.

Did you know? After David’s prayer, the entire assembly blessed the Lord, bowed their heads, and worshiped Him; in this way, the voluntary giving became a shared public act of prayer and thanksgiving.
Did you know? David reigned over Israel for forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
